paragraphs: Atlanta Braves Holdings, Inc. ("Atlanta Braves Holdings," "the Company," "us," "we," or "our") is primarily comprised of Braves Holdings, LLC ("Braves Holdings"), a wholly-owned subsidiary, and corporate cash.

On July 18, 2023, Liberty Media Corporation ("Liberty" or "Liberty Media"), the then current parent organization of the Company, completed the previously announced redemption of each outstanding share of its Liberty Braves common stock in exchange for one share of the corresponding series of common stock of a newly formed entity, Atlanta Braves Holdings (the "Split-Off"). The Split-Off was intended to be tax-free to holders of Liberty Braves common stock and in September 2024, the Internal Revenue Service completed its review of the Split-Off and notified Liberty that it agreed with the non-taxable characterization of the transaction.

The intergroup interests in the Liberty Braves Group held by subsidiaries of Liberty prior to the Split-Off were settled through attribution of Atlanta Braves Holdings Series C common stock and subsequently sold in the secondary market. Atlanta Braves Holdings did not receive any of the proceeds from the sale of our common stock by these subsidiaries of Liberty. Following this transaction, neither Liberty nor Atlanta Braves Holdings has any continuing stock ownership, beneficial or otherwise, in the other.

In connection with the Split-Off, Liberty and Atlanta Braves Holdings entered into certain agreements in order to govern certain of the ongoing relationships between the two companies after the Split-Off and to provide for an orderly transition. These agreements included a reorganization agreement, a services agreement, aircraft time sharing agreements, a facilities sharing agreement, a tax sharing agreement and a registration rights agreement. The facilities sharing agreement and aircraft time sharing agreements were terminated as part of the Corporate Governance Transition (as defined below).

The reorganization agreement provides for, among other things, the principal corporate transactions (including the internal restructuring) required to effect the Split-Off, certain conditions to the Split-Off and provisions governing the relationship between Atlanta Braves Holdings and Liberty with respect to and resulting from the Split-Off. The tax sharing agreement provides for the allocation and indemnification of tax liabilities and benefits between Liberty and Atlanta Braves Holdings and other agreements related to tax matters. Pursuant to the services agreement, Liberty provided Atlanta Braves Holdings with general and administrative services including legal, tax, accounting, treasury, information technology, cybersecurity and investor relations support. Atlanta Braves Holdings reimbursed Liberty for direct, out-of-pocket expenses and paid a services fee to Liberty under the services agreement that was subject to adjustment quarterly, as necessary. Additionally, pursuant to the services agreement with Liberty and prior to the Corporate Governance Transition (as defined below), components of Liberty's Chief Executive Officer's compensation were either paid directly to him or reimbursed to Liberty, in each case, based on allocations set forth in the services agreement. The allocation percentage was 7% for Atlanta Braves Holdings during the period from July 18, 2023 to December 31, 2023, and was 8% during the period from January 1, 2024 to August 31, 2024, when the Corporate Governance Transition (as defined below) occurred. On October 31, 2025, Atlanta Braves Holdings and Liberty mutually agreed to terminate the services agreement, as Atlanta Braves Holdings has fully assumed responsibility for the functions previously provided thereunder.

On August 21, 2024, Terence F. McGuirk ("McGuirk") entered into certain shareholder arrangements with Dr. John C. Malone ("Malone"), pursuant to which Malone granted McGuirk a proxy (the "Malone Voting Agreement") to vote 887,079 shares of the Company's Series B Common Stock owned by Malone, representing 44% of the Company's then outstanding voting power, on director elections, the approval or authorization of executive compensation and other routine matters. Malone also granted McGuirk a right of first refusal with respect to future transfers of the Company shares beneficially owned by Malone as well as certain appreciation rights with respect to the value of Malone's shares of Series B Common Stock. Additionally, Atlanta Braves Holdings and Liberty transitioned various general and administrative services provided by Liberty to the management of Atlanta Braves Holdings, including legal, tax, accounting, treasury, information technology, cybersecurity and investor relations support. As part of that transition, the then-current officers of the Company

(with limited exceptions) stepped down from their officer positions, effective August 31, 2024, and members of the Atlanta Braves Holdings operating team assumed these roles effective September 1, 2024 (the "Corporate Governance Transition").

paragraphs: An investment in our common stock involves risk. Before investing in our common stock, in addition to the other information described in Item 7 ("Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations") of Part II, you should carefully consider the following risks. Such risks are not the only ones that relate to our businesses and capitalization. The risks described below are considered to be the most material. However, there may be other unknown or unpredictable economic, business, competitive, regulatory or other factors that also could have material adverse effects on our businesses. Past financial performance may not be a reliable indicator of future performance and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods. If any of the events described below or in the documents incorporated by reference herein were to occur, our businesses, prospects, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows could be materially adversely affected, which in turn could have a material adverse effect on the value of our common stock.

Braves Holdings derives revenue directly from the sale of their local broadcasting rights through an individually negotiated carriage or license agreement. The sale of their national broadcasting rights, together with those of all other MLB Clubs, is organized through MLB with all such revenue allocated consistent with the MLB Rules and Regulations. A majority of this revenue is reliant on a limited number of broadcasting partners. Solvency and business disruptions impacting our broadcasting partners, as well as any decline in television ratings, carriage disputes, popularity of the Braves specifically, or even MLB as a whole, could adversely affect the revenue that can be derived from the sale of these broadcasting rights. There can be no assurance that upon the completion of local or national contractual arrangements that Braves Holdings or MLB will be able to successfully negotiate extensions or replacement deals that would provide similar amounts of revenue for Braves Holdings.

In recent years, certain regional sports networks have experienced financial difficulties. For example, in 2023 Diamond Sports Group, a subsidiary of Sinclair Broadcasting Group and parent of SportSouth which licenses and distributes sports content in various regional markets including the Braves games (other than nationally televised games), filed voluntary petitions for relief under Chapter 11 in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas. Diamond Sports Group completed its financial restructuring and emerged from bankruptcy effective January 2025 as Main Street Sports Group and provided all payments to Braves Holdings during bankruptcy and throughout the 2025 season. In late 2025 and early 2026, Main Street Sports Group continued to face financial difficulties culminating in the failure to make contractual payments to various professional sport clubs, including the Braves. As a result, the Braves terminated the Braves Broadcasting Agreement and recorded an impairment on the underlying long-term local broadcasting contract asset. In February 2026, the Braves announced BravesVision, a multimedia platform owned and operated by the Company that will become the local television home of the Braves beginning with the 2026 season. This new multimedia platform and its monetization of our local broadcasting rights may provide less revenue than what Braves Holdings previously received pursuant to the Braves Broadcast Agreement.

Our financial results depend in large part on the ability of the Braves to achieve on-field success. The team's successes generate significant fan enthusiasm, resulting in sustained ticket, premium seating, concession and merchandise sales, and greater shares of local television and radio audiences during that period. Furthermore, participation in MLB's postseason provides the franchise with additional revenue and income, primarily derived from games played at the Braves' home stadium. While the Braves did not make the postseason in 2025, the team appeared in 2 out of 18 potential postseason games in 2024 and 4 out of 18 potential postseason games in 2023. Revenue from postseason play (after reduction for allocable postseason share payments) was approximately $2.0 million and $11.3 million in 2024 and 2023, respectively. While the Braves have made the MLB postseason during nine of the past fourteen seasons, and were the 2021 World Series Champions, there can be no assurance that the team will perform well or qualify for postseason play during the next season or any season thereafter. Poor on-field performance by the Braves is likely to adversely affect our financial performance.

The success of the Braves depends, in large part, on the ability to develop, obtain and retain talented players. The Braves compete with other MLB baseball teams and teams in other countries for available professional players and top player prospects. There can be no assurance that the Braves will be able to retain players upon expiration of their contracts or identify and obtain or develop new players of adequate talent to replace players who retire or are injured, traded, released or lost to free agency. Even if the Braves are able to retain or obtain players who have had successful amateur or professional careers, or develop talented players through the Braves' minor league affiliates or otherwise, there can be no assurance that such players will perform successfully for the Braves.

The current market value of a given MLB player is subject to market conditions generally and more specifically based on the player's experience, position played, recent performance statistics, physical health, other similar players available at such time and other factors, such as the desirability of a particular franchise to such player, all of which vary over time. In general, player signings occur frequently enough that there are comparable objective data points that can be utilized in determining the value of a given MLB player. However, for top-ranked players, there may not be frequent enough player signings to provide sufficient recent comparable objective data points for valuation purposes. As a result, the Braves' ability to accurately determine the market value of a given player may be significantly impacted by Braves' subjective inputs and assumptions. Further, while a player's market value is generally determined at the time of signing, the evaluation of the contributions made by the player are ongoing throughout the life of the contract and the overall value of the entire contract can be analyzed only after the expiration of such contract. As a result, the Braves' ability to determine the market value of an MLB player is inherently uncertain, and the Braves may fail to assign a market value that is commensurate with such player's contributions over the life of the contract term. These challenges, and the related risk that the Braves may fail to accurately determine the market value of a given player, may be exacerbated as the length of the contract term increases. As a result, entry into long-term contracts, which generally include higher aggregate compensation, may increase the risk that the Braves fail to accurately determine the market value of a given player. The Braves' inability to accurately determine the market value of the players who are signed may negatively impact the ability of the Braves to achieve on-field success, which is likely to adversely affect our financial performance.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis provides information concerning our results of operations and financial condition. This discussion should be read in conjunction with our accompanying consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto.

On July 18, 2023, Liberty Media Corporation ("Liberty" or "Liberty Media"), the then current parent organization of Atlanta Braves Holdings, Inc. ("Atlanta Braves Holdings," "the Company," "us," "we," or "our") completed the previously announced redemption of each outstanding share of its Liberty Braves common stock in exchange for one share of the corresponding series of common stock of the Company (the "Split-Off"). The Split-Off was intended to be tax-free to holders of Liberty Braves common stock and in September 2024, the Internal Revenue Service completed its review of the Split-Off and notified Liberty that it agreed with the non-taxable characterization of the transaction. In September 2024, the then-current officers of the Company (with limited exceptions) stepped down from their officer positions and members of its wholly-owned subsidiary Braves Holdings, LLC ("Braves Holdings") assumed these roles (the "Corporate Governance Transition"). The Company is comprised of the businesses, assets and liabilities of its wholly-owned subsidiary Braves Holdings and corporate cash.

The intergroup interests in the Liberty Braves Group held by subsidiaries of Liberty prior to the Split-Off were settled through attribution of Atlanta Braves Holdings Series C common stock and subsequently sold in the secondary market. Atlanta Braves Holdings did not receive any of the proceeds from the sale of our common stock by these subsidiaries of Liberty. Following this transaction, neither Liberty nor Atlanta Braves Holdings has any continuing stock ownership, beneficial or otherwise, in the other.
The Company manages its business based on the following reportable segments: Baseball and Mixed-Use Development.

The Baseball segment includes operations relating to the Atlanta Braves Major League Baseball Club ("ANLBC," the "Atlanta Braves," the "Braves," the "club," or the "team") and the Braves' ballpark ("Truist Park" or the "Stadium") and includes revenue generated from ticket sales, concessions, local broadcasting rights, advertising sponsorships, suites and premium seat fees, retail and licensing revenue, shared Major League Baseball ("MLB") revenue streams, including national broadcasting rights and licensing, and other sources. Ticket sales, concessions, broadcasting rights and advertising sponsorship sales are the Baseball segment's primary revenue drivers.

The Mixed-Use Development segment includes retail, office, hotel and entertainment operations primarily within The Battery Atlanta and the surrounding area (the "Mixed-Use Development"). In April 2025, the Company, through a wholly-owned subsidiary completed the acquisition of certain real estate assets adjacent to The Battery Atlanta (the "Acquisition"). The Mixed-Use Development segment derives revenue primarily from office and retail rental income (including overage rent and tenant reimbursements) and, to a lesser extent, parking and advertising sponsorships throughout the year.

The financial results of Atlanta Braves Holdings depend in large part on the ability of the Braves to achieve on-field success. The team's successes generate significant fan enthusiasm, resulting in sustained ticket, premium seating, concession and merchandise sales, and greater shares of local broadcasting audiences. Management focuses on making operational and business decisions that enhance the on-field performance of the Braves and this may sometimes require implementing strategies and making investments that may negatively impact short-term profitability for the sake of immediate on-field success.

Braves Holdings, affiliated entities and third-party development partners, developed a significant portion of the land around Truist Park, the Braves' stadium, creating a 2.25 million square-foot mixed-use complex that features retail, residential, office, hotel and entertainment opportunities, known as The Battery Atlanta. We believe that the continued development and operations of The Battery Atlanta, as well as transactions such as the Acquisition, will result in increased game attendance as well as office and retail rental income (including overage rent and tenant reimbursements), and income from parking and corporate sponsorships throughout the year.

Atlanta Braves Holdings manages its business based on the following reportable segments: Baseball and Mixed-Use Development. The Baseball segment includes its operations relating to the Braves baseball franchise and Truist Park and includes revenue generated from game attendance (ticket sales), concessions, local broadcasting rights, advertising sponsorships, suites and premium seat fees, retail and licensing revenue, shared MLB revenue streams, including national broadcasting rights and licensing, and other sources.

The Mixed-Use Development segment includes retail, office, hotel and entertainment operations primarily within The Battery Atlanta and the surrounding area. The Mixed-Use Development segment derives revenue primarily from office and retail rental income (including overage rent and tenant reimbursements) and, to a lesser extent, parking and advertising sponsorships throughout the year.

The ability of Atlanta Braves Holdings to increase or maintain revenue and earnings could be adversely affected to the extent that relevant economic environments decline. Future performance is dependent in part on general economic conditions and the effect of those conditions on our customers. Weak economic conditions may lead to lower ticket demand for baseball events, which would also negatively affect concession and merchandise sales, and lower levels of advertising sponsorships. While Atlanta Braves Holdings is currently unable to predict the extent of any of these potential adverse effects as of December 31, 2025, Atlanta Braves Holdings does not believe that its operations have been materially impacted by recent economic pressures.

In late 2025 and early 2026, the parent of our local broadcasting partner, Main Street Sports Group, faced financial difficulties culminating in the failure to make contractual payments to various professional sport clubs, including the Braves. As a result, the Braves terminated the Braves Broadcasting Agreement and recorded a $30.1 million contract asset impairment associated with the long-term local broadcasting agreement within the Company's December 31, 2025 consolidated financial statements. In Februray 2026, the Braves announced BravesVision, a multimedia platform owned and operated by the Company that will become the official local television home of the Braves beginning with the 2026 season.

paragraphs: Atlanta Braves Holdings, Inc. ("Atlanta Braves Holdings," "the Company," "us," "we," or "our") 主要由 Braves Holdings, LLC ("Braves Holdings"), 一間百分之百持股的子公司，以及公司現金組成。

2023 年 7 月 18 日，Liberty Media Corporation ("Liberty" 或 "Liberty Media"), 當時本公司之母公司，完成先前公告的贖回所有 Liberty Braves 普通股，換取新成立實體 Atlanta Braves Holdings 對應系列普通股之一股，此為 "Split-Off"。Split-Off 旨在對 Liberty Braves 普通股持有人為稅務無負擔，2024 年 9 月，美國國稅局完成對 Split-Off 之審查，並通知 Liberty 同意該交易為非稅務負擔性質。

Split-Off 之前，Liberty 之子公司持有 Liberty Braves Group 之跨公司權益，透過歸屬 Atlanta Braves Holdings Series C 普通股並隨後在二級市場出售予以解決。Atlanta Braves Holdings 未從這些 Liberty 子公司出售我們普通股之所得中獲取任何收益。此交易後，Liberty 及 Atlanta Braves Holdings 皆無持續持有對方之股票，無論是否為受益所有權。
配合 Split-Off，Liberty 與 Atlanta Braves Holdings 籤訂若干協議，以規範兩家公司 Split-Off 後之持續關係，並提供有序過渡。這些協議包括重組協議、服務協議、飛機時段共享協議、設施共享協議、稅務共享協議及註冊權協議。設施共享協議及飛機時段共享協議已於公司治理過渡（如下所定）中終止。

重整協議包含多項內容，包括實現分拆（Split-Off）所需的主體企業交易（包括內部重整）、分拆的條件以及有關分拆後亞特蘭大勇士持有公司與自由企業之間關係的條款。稅收分擔協議則規範自由企業與亞特蘭大勇士持有公司之間稅務負擔與利益的分擔與賠償，以及與稅務相關的其他協議。根據服務協議，自由企業為亞特蘭大勇士持有公司提供一般及行政服務，包括法律、稅務、會計、財務、資訊科技、網路安全及投資者關係支援。亞特蘭大勇士持有公司為自由企業補償直接、實支費用，並根據服務協議支付服務費用，該費用每季調整一次，如需。此外，根據與自由企業的服務協議，並在企業治理過渡（如下所定）前，自由企業首席執行官薪酬的一部分，或是直接支付給他，或是補償給自由企業，視服務協議中所列的分攤比例而定。亞特蘭大勇士持有公司在2023年7月18日至2023年12月31日期間的分攤比例為7%，在2024年1月1日至2024年8月31日期間為8%，此為企業治理過渡（如下所定）發生時的分攤比例。2025年10月31日，亞特蘭大勇士持有公司與自由企業雙方同意終止服務協議，因亞特蘭大勇士持有公司已完全承擔此前由該協議提供的功能。

2024年8月21日，Terence F. McGuirk（"McGuirk"）與Dr. John C. Malone（"Malone"）簽訂若干股東協議，根據協議，Malone同意McGuirk代表其投票所持有的887,079股公司B系列普通股，代表當時公司流通在外投票權的44%，用於董事選舉、批准或授權高階管理層薪酬及其他常規事項。Malone亦同意McGuirk對未來Malone持有的公司股份轉讓享有優先購買權，以及針對Malone持有的B系列普通股價值的某些增值權。此外，亞特蘭大勇士持有公司與自由企業將由自由企業提供的多項一般及行政服務轉移至亞特蘭大勇士持有公司的管理層，包括法律、稅務、會計、財務、資訊科技、網路安全及投資者關係支援。作為此過渡的一部分，公司現任高階管理人員（有限例外情況除外）於2024年8月31日生效時辭去高階管理職務，亞特蘭大勇士持有公司的運營團隊成員則於2024年9月1日生效時接任這些職務（"企業治理過渡"）。
(除有限例外外) 已卸任其高階主管職位，自 2024 年 8 月 31 日起生效，並由亞特蘭大勇士持股公司營運團隊成員自 2024 年 9 月 1 日起接任這些職位(稱為 "公司治理過渡")。

paragraphs: 下列討論與分析提供有關我們營運成果與財務狀況之資訊。此討論應與我們附屬之合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。

2023年7月18日，Liberty Media Corporation（"Liberty" 或 "Liberty Media"），當時為Atlanta Braves Holdings, Inc.（"Atlanta Braves Holdings," "the Company," "us," "we," 或 "our"）之母公司，完成先前公告之Liberty Braves普通股每張現有股份兌換為本公司對應系列普通股之交易（"Split-Off"）。此Split-Off旨在對Liberty Braves普通股持有人為稅務無負擔之交易，2024年9月，美國國稅局完成對此Split-Off之審查，並通知Liberty同意此交易之非稅務性質。2024年9月，當時本公司之高層管理人（有限例外）卸任，其全資子公司Braves Holdings, LLC（"Braves Holdings"）之成員接任此職務（"企業治理過渡"）。本公司由其全資子公司Braves Holdings之業務、資產與負債以及公司現金組成。

Liberty先前持有Liberty Braves Group之跨集團權益，於Split-Off後透過發行Atlanta Braves Holdings Series C普通股進行結算，並隨後在二級市場出售。Atlanta Braves Holdings未從Liberty之子公司出售本公司普通股之所得中獲取任何收益。此交易後，Liberty與Atlanta Braves Holdings均無持續之股權、受益或其它形式之股權於對方。
本公司依下列應報告分部進行業務管理：棒球與混合用途開發。

棒球分部包含與亞特蘭大勇士大聯盟棒球俱樂部（"ANLBC," "亞特蘭大勇士," "勇士," "俱樂部," 或 "球隊"）及其球場（"Truist Park" 或 "球場"）相關之營運，包含由門票銷售、場內販賣、本地廣播權、廣告贊助、包廂與高級座位費用、零售與授權收入、共享大聯盟棒球（"MLB"）收入流，包括國家廣播權與授權，以及其他來源。門票銷售、場內販賣、廣播權與廣告贊助銷售為棒球分部之主要收入來源。
混合用途開發分部包含零售、辦公室、酒店與娛樂營運，主要位於The Battery Atlanta與周邊地區（"混合用途開發"）。2025年4月，本公司透過全資子公司完成對The Battery Atlanta周邊之部分不動產資產之收購（"收購"）。混合用途開發分部之收入主要來自辦公室與零售租金收入（包括過租收入與租戶補償），其次則為全年之停車與廣告贊助收入。
Atlanta Braves Holdings之財務表現很大程度取決於勇士隊在場上之成功表現。球隊之成功表現會產生大量球迷熱情，導致門票、高級座位、場內販賣與商品銷售持續增加，以及本地廣播觀眾份額提高。管理層專注於做出提升勇士隊場上表現之營運與商業決策，有時可能需要實施策略與進行投資，即使這會對短期利潤產生負面影響，以換取即時之場上成功。

Braves Holdings、相關機構與第三方開發夥伴開發了Truist Park周圍大量土地，創造出一個225萬平方呎之混合用途複合區，包含零售、住宅、辦公室、酒店與娛樂機會，稱為The Battery Atlanta。我們認為The Battery Atlanta之持續開發與營運，以及如收購之交易，將導致觀眾人數增加，以及全年辦公室與零售租金收入（包括過租收入與租戶補償），以及停車與企業贊助收入增加。
Atlanta Braves Holdings 依下列應報告分部來管理其業務：棒球與混合用途開發。棒球分部包括其與 Braves 棒球俱樂部及 Truist Park 相關的營運，並包含由觀眾入場（票務銷售）、場內販賣、地方廣播權、廣告贊助、包廂與高級座位費用、零售與授權收入、共享 MLB 收入流，包括國家廣播權與授權，以及其他來源產生的營業收入。
混合用途開發分部包括零售、辦公室、酒店與娛樂營運，主要位於 The Battery Atlanta 及周遭地區。混合用途開發分部的營業收入主要來自辦公室與零售租金收入（包括額外租金與租戶補償），並在較小程度上來自全年內的停車與廣告贊助。

Atlanta Braves Holdings 提高或維持營業收入與獲利的能力，可能因相關總體經濟環境衰退而受到不利影響。未來表現部分取決於總體經濟狀況以及這些狀況對我們客戶的影響。弱勢的經濟狀況可能導致棒球活動的入場需求減少，這也會對場內販賣與商品銷售產生負面影響，並降低廣告贊助的水準。儘管 Atlanta Braves Holdings 目前無法預測截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日任何這些潛在不利影響的程度，Atlanta Braves Holdings 不認為其營運已因近期經濟壓力而受到重大影響。

在 2025 年晚期與 2026 年初期，我們地方廣播夥伴的母公司 Main Street Sports Group 面臨財務困難，最終導致未能履行與各專業運動俱樂部（包括 Braves）的契約付款。因此，Braves 違約終止了 Braves 廣播協議，並在本公司 2025 年 12 月 31 日合併財務報表中記錄了 30.1 百萬美元的長期契約資產減損，與該長期地方廣播協議相關。在 2026 年 2 月，Braves 宣佈了 BravesVision，這是本公司擁有並營運的多媒體平台，將成為 Braves 2026 賽季起的官方地方電影片道。
總體說明。以下表格提供有關 Atlanta Braves Holdings 過去合併營運結果與其他收入與費用的資訊，以及這些項目來自我們應報告分部的貢獻。"公司與其他"類別包含那些不具備獨立應報告分部資格的資產。
有關我們 2025 財年財務狀況與營運結果與 2024 財年比較的討論，請參見下文。有關我們 2024 財年財務狀況與營運結果與 2023 財年比較的討論，請參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日為期終結的年度報告 Form 10-K 中的 Part II, Item 7. "管理層對財務狀況與營運結果的討論與分析"，該報告於 2025 年 3 月 3 日提交至 SEC。

paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及風險。在投資本公司普通股之前，除第二部分第 7 項（"管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析"）所描述之其他資訊外，您應謹慎考量下列風險。這些風險並非唯一與本公司業務及資本結構相關之風險。下列所描述之風險被認為是最重要者。然而，可能還有其他未知或無法預測之經濟、業務、競爭、法規或其他因素，也可能對本公司業務產生重大不利影響。過去之財務表現未必是未來表現之可靠指標，歷史趨勢亦不應用以預測未來期間之結果或趨勢。若下列或文中所引用文件中所述之任何事件發生，本公司業務、前景、財務狀況、營運結果及/或現金流可能受到重大不利影響，進而可能對本公司普通股價值產生重大不利影響。

Braves Holdings 的收入直接來自於其本地廣播權之銷售，透過個別協議或授權協議與電信業者達成。其全國廣播權之銷售，連同其他所有 MLB 球隊之廣播權銷售，則由 MLB 組織，所有相關收入依 MLB 規則與規範進行分配。此收入之大多數依賴於有限數量之廣播合作夥伴。若影響我們廣播合作夥伴之財務健全性與業務中斷，以及電視收視率下降、電信業者爭議、Braves 特別受歡迎程度，甚至 MLB 總體受歡迎程度，都可能對這些廣播權銷售所產生之收入造成不利影響。在完成本地或全國性合約安排後，Braves Holdings 或 MLB 並無保證能成功協商延長或替代合約，以提供與 Braves Holdings 前所獲得之收入相當之金額。

近年來，某些區域體育頻道曾面臨財務困難。例如，在 2023 年，Diamond Sports Group（Sinclair Broadcasting Group 旗下子公司，為 SportSouth 之母公司，授權與發行各區域市場之體育內容，包括 Braves 賽事（不包含全國電視轉播賽事））於美國德州南區地方法院提出根據第 11 章之財務重整申請。Diamond Sports Group 於 2025 年 1 月完成財務重整並從破產程序中脫離，成為 Main Street Sports Group，並在破產期間及 2025 賽季期間支付所有給 Braves Holdings 之款項。在 2025 年末及 2026 年初，Main Street Sports Group 繼續面臨財務困難，最終導致未能履行與各專業體育球隊（包括 Braves）之合約付款。因此，Braves 違約終止 Braves 廣播協議，並對其背後之長期本地廣播合約資產進行減值。2026 年 2 月，Braves 宣佈 BravesVision，為本公司擁有並營運之多媒體平台，將成為 Braves 2026 賽季起之本地電視主場。此新多媒體平台及其對本地廣播權之商業化，可能提供之收入少於 Braves Holdings 前所依據 Braves 廣播協議所獲得之收入。

我們之財務表現很大程度上取決於 Braves 之場上表現。球隊之成功會產生大量球迷熱情，導致持續之門票、VIP 座位、餐飲與商品銷售，以及該期間內較高的本地電視與廣播收視率。此外，參與 MLB 總決賽會為球隊帶來額外收入與收入，主要來自於在 Braves 主場所進行之賽事。雖然 Braves 在 2025 年未進入總決賽，但 2024 年參與 18 個潛在總決賽賽事中之 2 場，2023 年參與 18 個潛在總決賽賽事中之 4 場。總決賽賽事收入（扣除應分配之總決賽份額付款後）分別為 2024 年約 2.0 百萬美元及 2023 年約 11.3 百萬美元。雖然 Braves 在過去十四季中有九季進入 MLB 總決賽，並於 2021 年奪得世界大賽冠軍，但無法保證 Braves 在未來賽季或任何賽季中表現良好或取得總決賽資格。Braves 場上表現不佳將很可能對我們之財務表現造成不利影響。

Braves 之成功在很大程度上取決於開發、取得及留住優秀球員的能力。Braves 與其他 MLB 球隊及其他國家之球隊競爭可取得之專業球員與頂尖球員潛力。無法保證 Braves 能在合約到期時留住球員，或能識別並取得或培養足夠資質之新球員以取代退休、受傷、交易、解約或轉為自由球員之球員。即使 Braves 能留住或取得有成功業餘或職業生涯之球員，或透過 Braves 之小聯盟 affiliates 或其他方式培養出優秀球員，亦無法保證這些球員能在 Braves 有良好表現。

特定 MLB 球員之當前市場價值受一般市場條件影響，更特定地取決於球員之經驗、所屬位置、近期表現數據、身體健康、當時其他類似球員之可得性及其他因素，例如特定球隊對球員之吸引力，這些因素會隨時間而變化。通常，球員簽約頻率足夠，可提供可比之客觀數據點，以用於評估特定 MLB 球員之價值。然而，對於排名頂端之球員，可能缺乏足夠頻率之球員簽約，以提供足夠近期之可比客觀數據點，用以評估價值。因此，Braves 能準確評估特定球員之市場價值的能力，可能受到 Braves 主觀判斷與假設之重大影響。此外，雖然球員之市場價值通常在簽約時確定，但球員對球隊之貢獻評估會在合約期間持續進行，而整體合約價值只能在合約到期後進行分析。因此，Braves 能準確評估 MLB 球員之市場價值的能力本質上具有不確定性，Braves 可能未能為球員在其合約期間內之貢獻賦予相應之市場價值。這些挑戰，以及 Braves 可能未能準確評估特定球員之市場價值的相關風險，可能隨著合約期間延長而更加嚴重。因此，簽訂長期合約（通常包含較高總體薪酬）可能增加 Braves 未能準確評估特定球員之市場價值的風險。Braves 無法準確評估所簽約球員之市場價值，可能影響 Braves 達成場上成功之能力，進而很可能對我們之財務表現造成不利影響。
